title: 9 minutes to catch the last train — Part 2
style: Warm painterly 2D cartoon illustration, cinematic graphic-novel look: clean bold dark outlines, rich textured digital painting, soft volumetric light, deep warm oranges and moody blues, detailed environment, vertical 9:16 composition.
character: MAIN CHARACTER: a lanky ADULT man drawn as a minimalist cartoon: a perfectly round smooth tan head, two tiny solid black dot eyes set wide apart, short thin eyebrow strokes, a very small simple mouth, no nose, no visible hair, simple long limbs, dark charcoal baseball cap, oversized heather-grey hoodie, black slim pants, white sneakers. Minimal face like a webcomic, not a child, not anime, no big eyes.

scenes.A: The man sprinting down a station platform at night toward a train conductor in a uniform and cap standing by open train doors.
scenes.B: The train conductor holding the train door open with one arm, waving toward the stairs, the old man with a cane and his small dog hurrying onto the platform.
scenes.C: Inside a train carriage at night, the man and the old man with the small dog sitting across from each other laughing, city lights streaking past the window.
scenes.D: Next morning, a bright modern office, the man in a shirt walking into an interview room and freezing: the same old man sitting behind the desk with the small dog at his feet.
scenes.E: Close-up portrait of the man facing the viewer, shocked then grinning, bright office behind him.

segments.text: You reach the conductor with forty seconds left. One more passenger. He walks slowly. Please.
The conductor holds the doors. The old man and his dog make it on.
You talk the whole ride. About his dog. About your interview.
Next morning, you walk into the interview room.
Behind the desk: the old man. And the dog.
He says you already passed the only question that mattered. The end.
